status: Beats no skill and the comparison skill on total on both models, and is never worse on the three traps. Not fully at the bar: in the final round the grader found no major invented facts, but with-skill Opus made two small unsupported statements (it told Tallyhouse to 'add CAD' to $349/month, though the billing currency isn't stated anywhere; and it paraphrased Quillmetrics' trial FAQ as 'take payment when the trial ends'). Under the Standard's rule that a plausible guess counts as an invention, those keep it from 'Meets the Bench Standard bar'.
method: 8 evals (3 traps: asked to predict a conversion rate, no pages supplied, an already well-built page under pressure to buy an overhaul), 61 expectations written before any run. Round 1 ran the skill, no skill, and the comparison skill (Corey Haines' page-cro 1.1.0) on Haiku, and the skill and no skill on Opus, in fresh headless agents graded blind by a separate Opus grader. Round 2 re-ran the skill on Haiku (v1.1.0). Round 3 re-ran the skill on Haiku and Opus (v1.2.0).
losses_and_open_issues: Round 3, Haiku, eval 7 (Guided mode) 2/5: the run never read the supplied pages, taking the runner's 'read only this file' line to cover the project folder, and asked for pages it already had. Rounds 1-2 read them on the same prompt. Not fixed (round limit reached); a line saying Guided mode reads every page before pausing would address it
Round 1, Opus, eval 4: four suggestions on a sound page against a limit of three (plan items unlabelled); fixed in 1.1.0
Round 1, Haiku, eval 7: named a site-wide primary action instead of one per page; fixed in 1.1.0
Round 1: 4 with-skill replies named the skill, following the test machine's 'announce the skill' instruction; fixed in 1.1.0, none in rounds 2-3

Round 3, Opus: 'add CAD to $349/month' assumes a billing currency not stated; 'take payment when the trial ends' overstates the pricing FAQ; 'founder-led' for Pipewise on thin evidence (flagged as loose in the report)
Round 3, Haiku: rubric wording ('so the lower level applies') still appears in C1 evidence in two runs, and absolute run-folder paths appear in replies

Both models give C5 15/15 on the Tallyhouse landing page while flagging that the quote beside the form lacks naming permission: the C5 test is literal (proof present) and permission is reported as a finding, not a deduction
C1 on the Ferncliff pages differs between models (10 vs 0, nav 'Start free trial' against hero walkthrough): the rubric's 'competing' vs 'wording varies' boundary is loose

Round 1 without the skill: no-skill and page-cro runs gave worked lift maths or projected extra bookings (evals 2, 5), overwrote the earlier dim-conversion.json without a copy (eval 6), and page-cro invented a brand-file fact and said 'I used the page-cro skill' in most replies
Several expectations (C1-C6 scores, report file) measure the skill's format, so they are hard for no-skill configs by design; no-skill Opus found the core eval 1 problems but had no checklist score
